info.description: <app> · example vertical slice (widget CRUD + auth seam).

get.summary:
Admin session-hygiene report (`?window_minutes=`, default 60; the range
is `(0, 43200]` — go 422 → [`Error::Invalid`], 400).

parameters.name: window_minutes
parameters.description: Scan window in minutes; 60 by default

post.summary:
Admin: revoke every active session of one target user. A non-UUID id
revokes nothing (go lenient NULL behavior).

get.summary:
Admin: one target user's sessions (`?active_only=`, default true). A
non-UUID target id reads as an empty list (go lenient NULL behavior).

Fetch one user by id (go `uuidPtr` semantics: unknown or non-uuid → 404
from the service's parse gate).

put.summary: Update one user's flags/role (rank-gated + audited in the service).

post.summary:
Authed change: the current password is re-verified and every OTHER
active session is revoked — the caller's own survives via
`jti == sessions.id` (the verified token is re-read for its `jti`).

Request a reset code (rate-limited per email; unknown addresses read as
success — no existence leak).

200.description: Code sent when the account exists

302.description: Redirect to the frontend (success fragment or ?error= pairs)

get.summary:
Bearer-protected `{url}` whose state carries the link JWT (the
authenticated github connect flow).

200.description: The authorize URL carrying the link state

get.summary:
GET the github authorize URL when the provider is enabled (302); a
disabled/unconfigured provider answers the 403 envelope (operator
problem, not a redirect).

302.description: Redirects to the github authorize URL

post.summary:
Google One-Tap credential in, token pair out (cookie-mode cookie
included). Unconfigured provider answers 401 "google sign-in is not
configured".

401.description: Google sign-in unconfigured or token refused

post.summary:
Login: retry-lock + state gates; 200 with the token pair (and the
access-token cookie when cookie mode is on).

403.description: Account blocked, inactive, unverified or retry-locked

post.summary: Logout: revoke the given refresh token (idempotent) + clear the cookie.

put.summary: Partial profile update; returns the fresh row.

post.summary: Refresh: CAS rotation of the opaque token, fresh access token.

Consume the code + set the new password (auto-verify + optional
revoke-all).

get.summary: The caller's sessions, newest activity first.
The caller's most recent active session — `null` body when none.

post.summary: Revoke every active session of the caller.

Revoke the caller's CURRENT session: the access token's `jti` is the
session id (go parity), so the verified token is re-read for its `jti`
([`crate::auth::resolve_current_claims`]).

Register an account: unverified + a 6-digit code in the outbox. A
re-signup of an unverified address re-issues the code (201); a verified
address conflicts (409).

Unauthenticated bootstrap: a whitelisted email promotes its own account
to ADMIN. The empty whitelist disables the route entirely (403).

403.description: Email not whitelisted or the route disabled

post.summary: Check a code WITHOUT consuming it (go `Validate`).

400.description: Code invalid, used, expired or exhausted

post.summary:
Re-issue a fresh code (unknown + verified addresses read as success —
no existence leak).

200.description: A fresh code was sent (when the account exists)

get.summary:
SSE fan-out of the caller's private realtime room (go `widgets/events`
handler parity: `Subscribe(realtime.RoomUser(owner))`). Authenticated
(cookie) because browsers consume SSE via `EventSource`, which cannot set
headers. Yields an initial `retry: 2000`, then each hub frame as
`event: <type>`/`data: <json>` (`{"type","payload"}` with `payload`
omitted when null). Hub publishes never block (full buffer = drop), and a
disconnect is a normal exit — the dropped stream unsubscribes.

200.description: text/event-stream of the caller's room events; disconnect = unsubscribe

get.summary:
The `/ws` upgrade — handler inputs are passed through verbatim to
[`serve_ws`] (the shared JWT codec + the hub). Async by contract: axum
0.8 implements `Handler` only for future-returning fns — no awaits here.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Access token (query-raw; verified after the upgrade)

101.description: Upgrade accepted — the pump streams hub events (or closes 4001)

400.description: Not a websocket-upgrade request (axum extractor rejection)

get.summary:
Liveness — always succeeds, never touches the pool. Cheap for orchestrators
(k8s liveness probe) hammering it every few seconds.

Authenticated identity — returns the caller's id and roles. Protected by
`require_auth`; the `Principal` is set by the middleware from the verified
JWT. ponytail: a full security scheme (`bearer_auth`) should be registered on
this path when the login flow is built.

Readiness — actually probes the database (`SELECT 1`). Returns `200` when
the pool can serve, `503` with `status: "degraded"` when it cannot. This is
the probe that gates traffic: a failing DB means we are not ready.
Fetch a single widget by id.

put.summary:
Update an existing widget's mutable fields. `404` if the id does not exist
(update is NOT an upsert — it never creates a row).

delete.summary: Delete a widget by id. Idempotent — `404` only if the id never existed.

AdminUpdateUser.description:
go `api.AdminUpdateUser` parity — every field optional; an all-empty
patch is the go "invalid request".

role.description: DB role string; `""`/absent leaves the role untouched (go `""`).

AdminUser.description: go `api.AdminUser` parity (slice-local mapping, DB strings for enums).

AuthRefreshRequest.description:
go `api.AuthRefreshRequest` parity — the logout body carries the opaque
token too (go reuses the refresh shape).

AuthTokens.description: go `api.AuthTokens` parity — the login/refresh/oauth token pair.

upgraded.description: `false` reads as "the account already was an admin".

name.description: Human-readable name. Must not be blank.

EmailRequest.description:
go `api.EmailRequest` parity — verify/resend, forgot-password and the
upgrade-to-admin bootstrap all take just an address.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The JSON envelope returned to clients.

MeProfileResponse.description:
`GET /api/v1/auth/me` body — go `api.MeResponse` parity (slice-local
name: the router's legacy `/me` already owns `MeResponse`).
`phone_number`/`subscription` are NOT carried: the landed `core::User`
row has no such columns (see the route-parity deviations).

github_connected.description: go `GithubLinked` parity: linked ⇔ a non-empty github id.

MessageResponse.description: go `api.MessageResponse` parity — the uniform acknowledgement body.

Role.description: A caller's role. Drives every `can()` decision.

SessionItem.description: go `sessionItem` parity — one session row without its refresh token.

SignupRequest.description:
go `api.SignupRequest` parity — optional fields default to the empty
string, exactly as the go pointer-model decodes them (`user_type` is
passed through verbatim; the service normalizes it case-insensitively).

UpdateMeRequest.description:
go `api.UpdateMeRequest` parity — every field optional; maps 1:1 onto the
ports' [`UpdateMeInput`] under the go wire names.

name.description: Human-readable name. Must not be blank.

Widget.description: A domain entity — plain data, no behavior that needs the outside world.

WidgetId.description:
Strongly-typed id. A newtype around UUID prevents passing a `WidgetId`
where another id is expected — the compiler enforces it.

WidgetKind.description: A closed vocabulary. Mirror your DB enum here so the two never drift.
